title: Multiplication of arbitrary summable families in a nonarchimedean field
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value $|\cdot|:K\to\mathbf R_{\ge0}$, and give $K$ the metric $d(a,b)=|a-b|$. For arbitrary sets $I,J$, suppose $f:I\to K$ and $g:J\to K$ are summable, meaning their sums over finite subsets converge, with sums $a,b\in K$. Then the family $(f_i g_j)_{(i,j)\in I\times J}$ is summable with sum $ab$: $$\sum_{(i,j)\in I\times J}f_i g_j=\left(\sum_{i\in I}f_i\right)\left(\sum_{j\in J}g_j\right).$$ Completeness is not required. Empty and singleton index sets are allowed.

Positive-radius open balls around zero are additive subgroups by the strong triangle inequality; hence K has NonarchimedeanRing (its underlying NonarchimedeanAddGroup is the instance generated at Analysis/Normed/Group/Ultra.lean:192–200). No completeness or nontrivial-norm instance is needed.
